raw_case_text: Patient 1. A 72-year-old woman was admitted to hospital with (R) knee pain and swelling for 6/52. There are accompanying fever, night sweats, anorexia, and generalized body aches. She is known to have hypothyroid with osteoarthritis (OA) and polycythemia rubra vera. There was a history of raw milk ingestion. Her temperature was 38 C. The (R) knee was swollen, hot, and tender. General examination was normal except for splenomegaly. The WBC was 2.1 x 109 and platelets were 618 x 109 (150-450 x 109). CRP and uric acid were high at 55 mg/L (<5 mg/L) and 624 mumol/L (NR 143-339 mumol/L) consecutively. The differential diagnosis included septic arthritis and crystal arthropathy. X-ray showed moderate left knee osteoarthritis with mild effusion (Figure 1). Synovial fluid aspirate was exudative with protein 34 g/L and high LDH 1036 but was unsuitable for cell count. An initially negative brucella serology, 2 months ago, is now positive 1 : 10240 (Table 1). Blood culture x 6 was positive; however, echocardiogram did not reveal vegetations. After 3-month treatment of rifampicin and doxycycline her symptoms subsided and CRP is 12.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 72-year-old female presented with a 6-week history of right knee pain, swelling, fever, night sweats, anorexia, and generalized body aches.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed progressive right knee pain and swelling over a 6-week duration, accompanied by fever (38 °C), night sweats, anorexia, and generalized body aches. An initial serologic workup 2 months prior had been negative.
subjective.past_medical_history: Known history of hypothyroidism, osteoarthritis (OA), and polycythemia rubra vera. Epidemiological exposure: history of raw milk ingestion. Prior antibiotic therapy not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Right knee pain, swelling, fever, night sweats, anorexia, generalized body aches. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38 °C. Right knee: swollen, hot, and tender to palpation. Abdomen: splenomegaly. General physical examination otherwise normal.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC: 2.1 x 10^9/L (leukopenia); Platelets: 618 x 10^9/L (thrombocytosis, reference 150-450 x 10^9/L); CRP: 55 mg/L (reference <5 mg/L); Uric acid: 624 mumol/L (reference 143-339 mumol/L). Plain radiograph of knee: moderate osteoarthritis with mild joint effusion. Synovial fluid aspirate: exudative fluid with protein 34 g/L and LDH 1036 U/L (unsuitable for cell count).
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal, did not reveal vegetations.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Septic arthritis of the right knee and bacteremia due to Brucellosis (Brucella infection), occurring in a patient with underlying osteoarthritis and polycythemia rubra vera.
Confirmation: Brucella serology significantly positive at a titer of 1:10240 (seroconversion from negative serology 2 months prior); 6 out of 6 blood cultures positive for Brucella.
Differentials ruled out: Crystal arthropathy (gout) considered due to hyperuricemia (624 mumol/L); non-brucellar septic arthritis; infective endocarditis ruled out by negative echocardiography.
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with oral rifampicin and doxycycline for 3 months. Symptoms completely subsided, and follow-up CRP normalized to 12 mg/L.
